This is what lets a SAVED VIEW, a preset or an agent configure a grid: setColumnFilter(field, clause)  set one column's filter from a store FilterClause columnClause(field)            read it back — the same clause, for saving suspendColumnFilter(field, on) keep the clause but stop applying it clearColumnFilter(field?)      delete one, or all openColumnFilter(field, anchor) open that column's menu, anchored anywhere select(keys) / clearSelection() set the selection BY KEY (needs `key` in populate) actionsFor(count)              the actions that apply to a selection of that size — all of them for 1, only the `multi` ones for 2+, none for 0. A bulk toolbar reads this so it cannot disagree with the row menu selectedKeys / selectedRecords read it back

members.name: provide
members.description: Give this subtree its sources — and its Views. Every component already asking is answered again: a Context that swaps its source swaps it for everything in it. Settles once the kept Query, or the start View, is on.

members.name: open
members.description: Set up a page from its DEFINITION: its source over the app's store, every filter bar drawn from its scope — the View chip, the fields it holds, what it may add — and all of it provided. The source, or undefined for a page with no data.

members.name: close
members.description: Leave the page, or one still opening: its source goes, and nothing in the subtree reaches it.

members.name: saveView
members.description: Save what is on screen as a View of the open page, and put it on the View chip. With a name, a NEW View — a name any View has already gets ` - Copy-001`. With none, over the reader's own View on screen; a preset is never overwritten, so that answers undefined. The saved View's id, else undefined. `stay`: keep it for later, and stay on the View on screen — the save before a Reset all to default.

members.name: deleteView
members.description: Delete the reader's own View — the one on screen unless named — and go to the first. A preset is never deleted.

members.name: saveFilters
members.description: SAVE FILTERS — every scope's filters under one name, kept with the page beside its Views. With a name, that set — a set of the same name is saved over, so a host asks first. With none, over the set on screen; none on answers undefined. The set's id. Will, TODO 105.

members.name: applyFilters
members.description: APPLY a saved set: each scope it names takes its filters; Dismiss puts back what was on screen before the first one.

members.name: dismissFilters
members.description: DISMISS the set on screen: the filters go back as they were before it — or, for one saved from the screen, to the View's own. Never the sort.

members.name: deleteFilters
members.description: DELETE a saved set — the one on screen unless named. Its filters stay.

members.name: resetView
members.description: Put the filters back as the View on screen DEFINES them: the page's first Query, then the View's, as a pick puts it on. A filter the reader added since goes. What "Reset all to default" does.

members.name: export
members.description: This subtree's whole state as JSON — each source's question, and the View on screen — for a link, another service or an agent.

members.name: import
members.description: Take a state back in, exactly: each named source's question, and its View — shown on the View chip, and known to the pick listener, so the next pick of the old View is heard. A source it does not name is left as it is.

members.description: arrangeBy(field, direction) — steer a GROUP or SORT chip: its column, and for a sort which way. SILENT, like every steer. members.description: refresh() — redraw the FACE (value, tip, badge, condition) off the menu, once its rows have filled. For a host that set the rows SILENTLY: a steer fires no menu event, so the chip never heard it and kept a stale face. Never on or off — that stays the host's.

declarations.description: a run of controls in one direction, with a token gap. A layout surface: no chrome, fill, border or padding. Bordered box = sherpa-container; two-zone action strip = sherpa-toolbar.

attributes.name: data-align
attributes.description: start | center | end | stretch  | between — how items sit ACROSS the run (the cross axis), except `between`, which spreads them ALONG it

attributes.name: data-direction
attributes.description: block  | inline (a row)

attributes.name: data-fill
attributes.description: take the parent's height and hand the spare space to the child marked data-grow. Without it the stack is content-height and there is no spare space to give.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: sm (4) | md (8) | lg (12, default) | xl (16) | 2xl (24)

attributes.name: data-grow
attributes.description: with data-fill on the stack, this item takes the spare space and the others keep their natural size. Two attributes, not one: a stack cannot see its own children from CSS — `:host(:has(…))` does not parse, and `:host:has(…)` matches every host.

attributes.name: data-measure
attributes.description: cap the run's width at a reading measure (90ch) and centre it On a CHILD (not on the stack):

attributes.name: data-min-item
attributes.description: with data-wrap: hug — each item at its OWN width (a run of chips); else the floor an item may shrink to while it STRETCHES to share the line — sm (120) | md (200, default) | lg (280) | xl (360)

attributes.name: data-scroll
attributes.description: the run scrolls when it is taller than its room, instead of pushing the page. It caps the stack at its parent's height, so the parent must have one.

attributes.name: data-wrap
attributes.description: inline only: items wrap and share the line
